clue.text: Twist, having the savvy to grab right man

indicators.note: to grab means one piece takes hold of another, enclosing it

parts.note: savvy, as a noun, is wit or shrewdness
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: Someone sharp enough to pick the right man for a job.
explanation.definitionFit: To writhe is to twist and squirm, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Birdman?

parts.note: split the word in two: a bird that is also a man on a chessboard, the castle piece

explanation.walkthrough: 'Birdman' suggests an aviator or bird fancier, but read it as bird plus man: a black crow-like bird that shares its name with a chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a crow-family bird and the chess piece also called the castle, a double sense packed into one word.

clue.text: Diplomacy gives free entry to your first and last animal with three toes

indicators.note: giving entry to means letting a piece in, so one word goes inside another

parts.note: tact is diplomacy, tactful handling
to rid is to free or clear

indicators.note: first means take the opening letter of the word your
last means take the final letter of the word animal

explanation.surface: Diplomacy grants your first and last beast passage, apparently a three-toed one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diplomacy' and 'free' sit side by side in the surface, but one is cut open by the other; the word 'gives' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Tridactyl is a zoological term meaning having three digits, here toes.

clue.text: If it's closed, you can't see priest you once introduced to daughter

definitions.text: If it's closed, you can't see

indicators.note: introduced to means one piece is inserted into the other

parts.note: Eli is the Old Testament priest who raised Samuel
ye is the archaic form of you

explanation.surface: A riddle about a cleric once presented to a daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: shut this fold of skin over the eye and sight is blocked.

clue.text: Wild trees of questionable identity, reportedly first encountered beside old railway line

indicators.note: reportedly means the word is as heard, so a sound-alike spelling is entered

parts.note: which? asks which one, querying identity

indicators.note: first encountered means take the opening letter of encountered

parts.note: LMS was the London, Midland and Scottish Railway, a pre-1948 British company

explanation.surface: Mysterious trees spotted next to a disused railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: LMS was one of Britain's big four railway companies before nationalisation in 1948.
explanation.definitionFit: Wych elms are native elms growing wild in British woodland, so wild trees.

clue.text: Goodwill shown by getting close to pay attention about painting headland

parts.note: warm, as in a guessing game, means getting close

indicators.note: about means one piece goes around the other

parts.note: to heed is to pay attention
painting is an example of art
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness

explanation.surface: Kindness displayed by focusing on a landscape painting of a cape.
explanation.definitionFit: Warmheartedness is kindly feeling towards others, the same as goodwill.

clue.text: Like early morning hedges, with horse, very black, sheltered by soaring tree

parts.note: a cob is a sturdy short-legged horse

indicators.note: sheltered by means one piece sits inside the other
soaring in a down clue means the word reads upwards, so tree goes backwards

parts.note: yew is a tree
BB marks a very soft, very black pencil lead

explanation.surface: A rural description of a horse and a dark tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Pencil leads are graded by softness, and the softest, blackest grades carry multiple Bs, so very black is a crossword convention; in a down clue 'soaring' means the tree reads bottom to top, giving WEY.
explanation.definitionFit: Hedges at dawn are often draped with dew-covered spiders' webs, so they look full of webs.

clue.text: Somewhere between nuisances boredom sets in

indicators.note: somewhere within the words between nuisances lies a run of letters to pull out

explanation.surface: Tedium creeps in between one annoyance and the next.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is a French borrowing meaning listless boredom.

clue.text: Trading jargon after Queen is swallowed by distance

indicators.note: being swallowed means going inside something else

parts.note: a mile is a distance

indicators.note: after means the jargon piece follows the Queen piece

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword Queen
cant is jargon, the special talk of a group

explanation.surface: Business-speak following royalty gets lost over the miles.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercantile means relating to merchants and trade, an adjectival synonym.

clue.text: Hold sway over go-getter claiming what's not yours

indicators.note: claiming means taking something in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a doer is an active go-getter
what is not yours is mine

explanation.surface: An ambitious type grabbing other people's property.
explanation.definitionFit: To domineer is to rule arrogantly, to hold sway over others.

clue.text: Two-fold dissembling by Iran

indicators.note: dissembling means disguising, so these letters are disguised by rearrangement

explanation.surface: Iran is accused of double-dealing deceit.
explanation.definitionFit: Binary means made of two parts, twofold.

clue.text: Touching figures cast to charm Letitia? Is it art, Michael?

indicators.note: cast suggests casting or shaping anew, so the letters are remoulded

explanation.surface: A spell cast on Letitia prompts a query to Michael about whether it is art.
explanation.walkthrough: The closing question to Michael is surface colour only and gives no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Arithmetical means concerning numbers, touching on figures.

clue.text: Person of taste of a sort uncomfortable with little fellow about

indicators.note: about means one piece is placed around the other

parts.note: a gnome is a little man of folklore

indicators.note: uncomfortable suggests something ill at ease, so these letters are shifted

explanation.surface: A connoisseur of sorts ill at ease with a small chap nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Person of taste' sounds like an aesthete, but here taste is the palate; 'uncomfortable' tells you to rearrange A SORT, giving ASTRO.
explanation.definitionFit: A gastronome is a connoisseur of good food, a person of refined taste.

clue.text: Old sailor's preserve

definitions.meaning: to ... meat or fish is to cure and preserve it

explanation.surface: An ancient mariner's jam.
explanation.definitionFit: One word for a veteran seaman and for curing food with brine.

clue.text: Mum's back, but cut short overdue walk

indicators.note: back means the word for mum is read backwards

parts.note: ma is mum

indicators.note: cut short means the final letter is lopped off

parts.note: taken as written before trimming
overdue means late

explanation.surface: Mum has returned, yet a long-delayed stroll is curtailed.
explanation.definitionFit: To ambulate is a formal word for to walk.

clue.text: When displayed are golden, as rabbits are

indicators.note: displayed means set out in a new arrangement, so the letters are laid out afresh

explanation.surface: Rabbits shown off with golden coats.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabbits are typically described as having long ears, a descriptive definition.

clue.text: Hot artist put up resistance to girl raised by an old witch

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

indicators.note: put up in a down clue means the word reads upwards, so artist runs backwards

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is the crossword artist
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the word for girl reads upwards

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana

explanation.surface: A heated painter resists a girl brought up by a crone.
explanation.definitionFit: A harridan is a bossy, scolding old woman, a hag or old witch.

clue.text: Stout little girl grabs touslehead with skin blemish

indicators.note: grabs means one piece takes hold of the other, enclosing it

parts.note: Sal is a short form of the girl's name Sally
the head, or first letter, of tousle is T
a wart is a skin blemish

explanation.surface: A plump young girl with messy hair and a wart.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalwart means sturdy and strongly built, a sense of stout.

clue.text: Nothing east of the river

parts.note: nil means nothing
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: There is nothing to the east of the river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nile is the great river of Egypt, the river par excellence.

clue.text: Research student in drag apt to use deception

indicators.note: deception suggests the letters disguising their true order

explanation.surface: A doctoral candidate in drag prone to trickery.
explanation.definitionFit: A postgraduate studies after a first degree, often doing research.

clue.text: Stomach about 60 minutes of the Fringe

indicators.note: about means one piece goes around the other

parts.note: tum is an informal word for stomach
sixty minutes is an hour, abbreviated HR

explanation.surface: A stomach rumbling for an hour at the Edinburgh Fringe.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fringe looks like the Edinburgh arts festival, but it means a loose edging of threads.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrum is a loose thread end on a loom, and thrums form a fringe.

clue.text: Hurried off to voice complaint

indicators.note: to voice means to say out loud, so a sound-alike spelling is entered

parts.note: flu is a complaint, an illness

explanation.surface: Someone rushed off to make a complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaint' reads as a grievance, but it is an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Flew means went quickly, hurried off, past tense to match.

clue.text: Stupid coming back to catch bishop with one: not nice

indicators.note: to catch means one piece encloses the other
coming back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: d'oh! is the exclamation for something stupid
RR, Right Reverend, is a bishop's title
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A fool returns to nab a bishop and someone else: unpleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming back' turns DOH into HOD, which holds RR and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Horrid means unpleasant, a direct synonym of not nice.

clue.text: Enchantress sent round lake, following directions to close in

indicators.note: following means the enchantress piece comes after the directions piece

parts.note: E and N, east and north, are compass directions

indicators.note: sent round means one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: Circe is the enchantress of Homer's Odyssey

explanation.surface: A sorceress sent around a lake on instruction to move in.
explanation.definitionFit: To encircle is to surround, to close in on all sides.

clue.text: What someone destitute is on?

parts.note: the idiom says a penniless person is on these, the timbers of a ship heeled over

explanation.definitionFit: Being on one's beam-ends is an idiom for being destitute, from a ship lying on its side.

clue.text: Settles every quarter to hold party

indicators.note: to hold means one piece contains the other

parts.note: all four compass quarters, east, north, west and south
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Arranging a celebration on all sides.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow is to settle money or property on someone.
